Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5366; unavaricious:--without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.
BiblicalUsage: Without covetousness — a bishop must not be greedy of filthy lucre, and every believer's manner of life is to be without covetousness, content with such things as we have. The word is freedom from the love of money.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe contentment is the other side of this word: God has said he will never leave me, and that is enough.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
